✨ AI Explanation for CRITICAL — select-name
What it means

A <select> element on the page lacks an accessible name, meaning screen readers cannot identify its purpose to users with disabilities.

Why it matters

Without an accessible name, users relying on assistive technology cannot interact with the form element, violating accessibility standards and potentially excluding a portion of the audience.

HIGH color-contrast via axe-core

Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

https://cityhangaround.com/

✨ AI Explanation for HIGH — color-contrast
What it means

The text or other foreground elements on the homepage do not have enough contrast against their background colors to meet WCAG 2 AA guidelines. This means the color difference is too low for many users to read comfortably.

Why it matters

Low contrast can make content unreadable for people with visual impairments, color blindness, or in bright lighting conditions. It also violates accessibility standards, potentially leading to legal issues and a negative user experience.

Recommended fix

Adjust the foreground or background colors so that the contrast ratio is at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Use a contrast checker tool to verify compliance and update the CSS accordingly.

HIGH scrollable-region-focusable via axe-core

Ensure elements that have scrollable content are accessible by keyboard in Safari

https://cityhangaround.com/

✨ AI Explanation for HIGH — scrollable-region-focusable
What it means

A scrollable area on the site is not keyboard‑navigable in Safari, meaning users who rely on the keyboard cannot access or interact with its content.

Why it matters

Keyboard users, including those with motor disabilities, will be unable to reach or read the scrollable content, violating accessibility guidelines and reducing overall usability.

Recommended fix

Wrap the scrollable content in a focusable element (e.g., add tabindex="0"), provide appropriate ARIA roles or labels, and ensure that keyboard focus can enter and exit the region. Test in Safari to confirm the area is reachable via the keyboard.

    MEDIUM region via axe-core

    Ensure all page content is contained by landmarks

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — region
    What it means

    The page contains content that is not enclosed within ARIA landmark elements such as <header>, <nav>, <main>, <footer>, or <aside>. Landmarks provide a way to identify major sections of a page.

    Why it matters

    Without landmarks, users of assistive technologies cannot quickly jump between sections, leading to a slower and more frustrating experience. It also reduces the overall accessibility score of the site.

    Recommended fix

    Add appropriate landmark elements around each major section of the page. For example, wrap the top navigation in <nav>, the main content in <main>, and the footer in <footer> to give clear structure.

    What it means

    HIGH

    Slow TTFB: Root document took 610 ms

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for HIGH — finding
    What it means

    The time to first byte (TTFB) for the root document is 610 ms, which is considered slow for a high‑performance website.

    Why it matters

    A high TTFB delays the start of page rendering, leading to slower perceived load times for users, especially on mobile or slower networks. It can negatively impact SEO rankings and user satisfaction.

    Recommended fix

    Optimize server response by enabling caching, reducing server processing time, and using a content delivery network (CDN). Consider upgrading hosting resources or optimizing backend code to lower the TTFB below 200 ms.

    HIGH

    Poor LCP: 6.6 s

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for HIGH — finding
    What it means

    The Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) metric measures how long it takes for the main content of a page to become visible to the user. A value of 6.6 seconds indicates that the page’s most significant visual element is taking far longer than recommended to load.

    Why it matters

    Slow LCP can frustrate visitors, increase bounce rates, and negatively impact search engine rankings, as search engines use LCP as a ranking signal. It also reduces the likelihood of users staying on the site long enough to engage with content or complete desired actions.

    Recommended fix

    Improve LCP by optimizing large images or text blocks (compress, resize, or use modern formats), removing render‑blocking CSS/JS, implementing lazy loading for off‑screen resources, and leveraging a CDN or server‑side caching to reduce load times. Additionally, consider deferring non‑essential scripts and ensuring the critical rendering path is streamlined.

    HIGH missing-hsts via header-analysis

    Missing HSTS header

    💡 Add strict-transport-security header to improve security

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for HIGH — missing-hsts
    What it means

    The site does not send a Strict‑Transport‑Security (HSTS) header, meaning browsers are not instructed to enforce HTTPS for future requests.

    Why it matters

    Without HSTS, users are vulnerable to downgrade attacks that force them to connect over HTTP, exposing sensitive data. It also reduces trust signals for visitors and can impact search rankings.

    Recommended fix

    Configure the web server to send the header: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload. This forces browsers to use HTTPS for the next 2 years and includes subdomains.

    HIGH missing-csp via header-analysis

    Missing CSP header

    💡 Add content-security-policy header to improve security

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for HIGH — missing-csp
    What it means

    The site does not send a Content‑Security‑Policy (CSP) header in its HTTP responses. CSP tells browsers which resources are allowed to load and execute, helping to block malicious code injection.

    Why it matters

    Without CSP, attackers can more easily inject or execute cross‑site scripting (XSS) payloads, potentially stealing user data or hijacking sessions. It also reduces the ability to mitigate other injection attacks and limits the effectiveness of other security controls.

    Recommended fix

    Add a CSP header that defines trusted sources, e.g. `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';` and adjust as needed for your site’s assets. Test the policy in report‑only mode before enforcing to avoid breaking legitimate content.

    MEDIUM 10020 via owasp-zap

    Missing Anti-clickjacking Header

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — 10020
    What it means

    The site is missing an anti‑clickjacking header such as X‑Frame‑Options or CSP frame‑ancestors. These headers prevent the page from being embedded in a frame or iframe on another site.

    Why it matters

    If the page can be framed, attackers can overlay malicious content on top of the legitimate page, tricking users into clicking on hidden buttons or links (clickjacking). This can lead to unauthorized actions or credential theft.

    Recommended fix

    Add an anti‑clickjacking header, for example `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` or a CSP directive `frame-ancestors 'self';`. Ensure the header is sent with all responses that render the page.

    MEDIUM 10038 via owasp-zap

    Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — 10038
    What it means

    The audit detected that a Content‑Security‑Policy header is not present in the site’s responses. CSP is a key defense against XSS and data injection attacks by restricting resource loading.

    Why it matters

    Without CSP, attackers have a broader attack surface to inject malicious scripts or steal sensitive information. It also weakens the overall security posture and can lead to compliance issues for sites handling user data.

    Recommended fix

    Implement a CSP header that specifies allowed sources for scripts, styles, images, etc. Start with a restrictive policy in report‑only mode, review the reports, and then enforce the policy once it no longer blocks legitimate content.

    MEDIUM 90003 via owasp-zap

    Sub Resource Integrity Attribute Missing

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — 90003
    What it means

    The page loads external resources such as scripts or stylesheets without specifying a Subresource Integrity (SRI) attribute. This means the browser cannot verify that the resource has not been altered since it was published.

    Why it matters

    Without SRI, an attacker who compromises a CDN or intercepts traffic could inject malicious code into the resource, potentially leading to cross‑site scripting or other attacks that affect all visitors.

    Recommended fix

    Add an integrity attribute with a cryptographic hash (e.g., SHA‑256) to each external script or stylesheet tag, and include the crossorigin attribute if the resource is served from a different origin.

    MEDIUM missing-x-content-type-options via header-analysis

    Missing X-Content-Type-Options header

    💡 Add x-content-type-options header to improve security

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — missing-x-content-type-options
    What it means

    The server does not send the X‑Content‑Type‑Options header, which instructs browsers not to MIME‑sniff content types.

    Why it matters

    Without this header, browsers may incorrectly interpret a file’s MIME type, allowing an attacker to trick the browser into executing malicious content as a script or other executable type, increasing the risk of XSS attacks.

    Recommended fix

    Configure the web server to include the header `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` in all responses.

    MEDIUM missing-x-frame-options via header-analysis

    Missing X-Frame-Options header

    💡 Add x-frame-options header to improve security

    https://cityhangaround.com/

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — missing-x-frame-options
    What it means

    The site does not send the X‑Frame‑Options header, so it can be embedded inside an iframe on other domains.

    Why it matters

    Embedding the site in an iframe can enable clickjacking attacks, where a malicious site tricks users into interacting with hidden or disguised content, potentially exposing sensitive actions or data.

    Recommended fix

    Add the header `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` or `DENY` to prevent framing, or use a Content Security Policy `frame-ancestors` directive to restrict which origins may embed the site.

    MEDIUM sensitive-url via crawl-analysis

    URL may contain sensitive data: https://cityhangaround.com/forgot-password

    https://cityhangaround.com/forgot-password

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — sensitive-url
    What it means

    The URL path for the forgot‑password page may expose sensitive information, such as user identifiers or tokens, in the browser address bar or server logs.

    Why it matters

    Sensitive data in URLs can be inadvertently shared through browser history, referrer headers, or server logs, increasing the risk of credential leakage or phishing attacks.

    Recommended fix

    Change the form to submit via POST and avoid including any sensitive parameters in the URL. Use a secure, single‑use token sent in the request body or as a cookie, and redirect to a generic confirmation page after submission.

    MEDIUM sensitive-url via crawl-analysis

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — sensitive-url

    MEDIUM multiple-h1

    Multiple H1 tags found (4)

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — multiple-h1
    What it means

    The page contains four H1 tags instead of a single top‑level heading. This indicates that multiple elements are marked as the main heading of the content.

    Why it matters

    Search engines use the H1 to understand the primary topic of a page; having several can dilute that signal and confuse crawlers. It can also affect accessibility, as screen readers rely on a single H1 to orient users.

    Recommended fix

    Replace the extra H1 tags with H2 or H3 elements, keeping only one H1 that accurately describes the page’s main topic. Ensure the remaining headings follow a logical hierarchy.

    MEDIUM missing-canonical

    No canonical URL specified

    ✨ AI Explanation for MEDIUM — missing-canonical
    What it means

    The page does not include a canonical link element, so search engines have no explicit indication of the preferred URL for this content.

    Why it matters

    Without a canonical tag, duplicate or similar pages may be indexed separately, splitting ranking signals and potentially causing search engine penalties. It also makes it harder to manage link equity across variations of the URL.

    Recommended fix

    Add a canonical tag in the head section: <link rel="canonical" href="https://cityhangaround.com/">. Verify that the URL matches the primary page you want indexed.
